::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Custom equations' names](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/4925/custom-equations-names), asked by [Abramo](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/1552/abramo) on TeX Stack Exchange (2010-11-04; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> Do you know how I can call a reference to an equation using `\ref` or `\eqref` and obtain the `(name of the equation)` instead of the standard counter?
:::

If you use the `amsmath` package you can do

```latex
\begin{equation}
  \tag{*}
  \int_{\partial\Omega} \omega = \int_\Omega d\omega
  \label{eqn:Stokes}
\end{equation}

By \eqref{eqn:Stokes} ...
```

Is that what you want?
